Dimana dalam transportasi terdapat dua unsur penting ialah: 1. Pemindahan. 2. Secara fisik terjadi pemindahan komoditas dan penumpang dari suatu tempat ke lokasi lain. Dalam transportasi terdapat dua golongan utama : 1) Pemindahan bahan-bahan dan hasil produksi dilaksanakan dengan memakai alat angkut. 2) Mengangkut manusia dari suatu tempat ke tempat lain. Hal yang sama juga disampaikan oleh Rustian Kamaludin (1986), bahwa transportasi adalah membawa suatu lokasi ke daerah yang lain atau dengan kata lain yaitu sebuah mobilitas komoditas atau manusia dari sebuah daerah ke lokasi lainnya. Selain itu menurut Rustian Kamaludin (1986), keuntungan dari adanya transportasi dapat dibagi menjadi dua komponen yakni: 1. Nilai guna lokasi (Place Utility) Yaitu penambahan nilai ekonomi atau nilai guna dari sebuah komoditi yang diciptakan dan memindahkannya dari sebuah daerah ke wilayah lain yang mempunyai nilai kegunaan yang lebih kecil, ke daerah dimana benda tersebut memiliki nilai kegunaan yang lebih banyak yang biasanya dievaluasi menggunakan uang (interens of money). 2. Nilai guna waktu (Time Utility) Yaitu kemampuan suatu barang untuk mengkover kebutuhan manusia dengan menghadirkan barang-barang, bukan cuma pada hal yang mereka membutuhkannya, namun pada hal yang mereka harapkan juga.

Deauthentication attack and other wifi hacks using an ESP8266 module.

I thought this was an attack against the ESP8266 from the title. Which means I pretty much misread it. But I am wondering if these modules will become more ubiquitous in small devices and what kind of exploits will be found that target them. They're closed source with a monolithic micro-OS block running on one core of the processor (leaving the other free for what the user/OEM programs on it). Someone is going to find some good poop on these things...

ESP8266 can be self programmed just like an Arduino. Actually you can use the Arduino editor to custom program them.

Programming them is actually surprisingly simple to do and does not even need the cloud or Internet connection. They can be their own be their own server, their own hotspot.....

But where do you store the biog web pages? There is not enough storage. Easily, Take an USB drive and store it on there. Or better for performance take a Wifi router that is not connected to the Internet and stick an USB dongle in there. Your ESP8266 only needs to store a redirection page to your local wifi based web server. No cloud or Internet connection required.

For those interested and get confused by the words;

ESP8266 is the chip that contains the wifi module. It is very similar Like the Arduino processor a,d can be programmed identically like the Arduino (just different compiled assembler)

ESP-12 is just a certain tiny motherboard that contains voltage regulator, memory and predefined pins. This is exactly like and Arduino board.

ESP-12 would be similar like an Arduino Mega; ESP-10 would be like an Arduino Uno, ESP-8 would be like an Arduino nano. ESP comes from the company NodeMCU as far as I recall correctly, it is the company that took an ESP8266 and put it on a specific print board

But you have different variations of print boards by different companies but they all use the same ESP8266.

In a lot of cases this ESP8266 module is connected to an Arduino so the Arduino can handle Wifi too. What they do is they take a firmware binary already made by some Open source project and upload it to that ESP8266. From now on you can communicate between the Arduino and the ESP8266 using simple serial communication and AT commands.

Interesting is that if you hook such an ESP-12 to your PC you basically create the same serial communication (through USB) and do the exact same AT commands through your console.

Do you need a lot to develop for this? No just an USB cable hook it to the ESP-12 module and that will power it and give you serial communication access to this device to be programmed. See it as an Arduino nano with limited digital IO pins but has the ability to communicate using Wifi.

The big bonus of all this is that you do not need to even use the Wifi at all. It is available in chip but you can perfectly us it as a none-wifi connected Arduino nano. Actually now that the Arduino Nano is not produced anymore this ESP82266 can perfectly replace it.

It took a lot of time to figuring it all out. But the breakthrough came when I realized that it is just another type of Arduino only different pin layouts and processor.

The danger of IoT is indeed a big issue when people upload a custom made firmware that connect to the Internet and therefor knows your login and password of your router. The other danger is when they are used into the cloud connected refrigerator and smart TV. That firmware may do other stuff like spying on you.
